answer: To defend an agent network from sybil swarms, nodes route messages along a verifiable trust thread rooted in bonded hardware enclaves. Each newly registered entity must light an inspection lantern by locking an unrefundable collateral deposit that scales quadratically with identity count. When malicious actors attempt to submerge the protocol under an ocean of puppet accounts, the compounding quadratic bond requirements force rapid capital exhaustion, making mass identity replication economically catastrophic while honest nodes only pay a flat linear setup fee.
